name: Hesiod
description: The poet of origins: the Theogony is the canonical account of cosmogony and divine genealogy, from Chaos to the reign of Zeus. The default lens for the core sky.

name: Homer
description: The oldest voice: the Olympians in action around the Trojan War and its aftermath. Frequently disagrees with Hesiod on parentage (Aphrodite, Hephaestus).

name: Pseudo-Apollodorus
description: The systematic mythographer: a compact encyclopedia of nearly the whole mythological tradition, often recording multiple variants side by side.

name: Apollonius of Rhodes
description: The epic of Jason and the Argonauts: the richest source for the Argonaut cycle and Hellenistic shadings of the gods.

name: Ovid
description: The Roman reteller: transformation stories with strong literary license; the source of many now-famous versions (Medusa, Arachne) absent from older Greek accounts.

name: Hyginus
description: The cataloguer: terse summaries and lists preserving many otherwise-lost variants, plus the star myths behind the constellations.

name: Pausanias
description: The traveller: local cult traditions and regional variants seen on the ground, often contradicting the Panhellenic poets.
